## What the method does

Huang et al. turn a gene expression profile into one pathway deregulation score (PDS) per
pathway with pathifier, fit a Cox model with an L1 (LASSO) penalty to the scores to select a few
prognostic pathways, and split tumours into higher and lower risk of relapse by the model's
prognostic index. The same steps work on clinical features, or on both together.

Huang S, Yee C, Ching T, Yu H, Garmire LX. A novel model to combine clinical and pathway-based
transcriptomic information for the prognosis prediction of breast cancer. *PLoS Comput Biol*
10(9):e1003851 (2014). doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003851.

## Install

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("jeonglab-bcm/fossil/PMC4168973/package")
```

```{r load}
library(pdscox)
packageVersion("pdscox")
```

## Example input

Two examples ship with the package. The first is the paper's training set: the clinical table of
the 236 Uppsala tumours with a relapse status. The paper counts the two patients without a
relapse time as time 0 and the tumours without p53 status as wild type; so do we.

```{r clinical}
clin <- read.csv(example_path("miller_clinical.csv"))
dim(clin)
head(clin)
clin$time[is.na(clin$time)] <- 0
clin$p53[is.na(clin$p53)] <- 0
```

The second is synthetic: 150 tumours, three gene sets of 12 genes and 40 background genes. Sets
A and B carry relapse risk (true log hazard ratios 1.0 and 0.7); set C does not.

```{r synthetic}
expr <- as.matrix(read.csv(example_path("synthetic_expression.csv"), row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
surv <- read.csv(example_path("synthetic_survival.csv"))
sets <- read_gmt(example_path("synthetic_sets.gmt"))
dim(expr)
lengths(sets)
table(relapse = surv$event)
```

## Run the method

Pathway deregulation scores, then the Cox-LASSO model. The paper ran 250 cross-validation runs to
choose the penalty; 20 are enough here.

```{r pds, results = "hide"}
pds <- pathway_scores(expr, sets, attempts = 20)
```

```{r model}
model <- cox_lasso(t(pds), surv$time, surv$event, runs = 20)
round(model$coefficients, 3)
pi <- prognostic_index(model$coefficients, t(pds))
res <- evaluate_model(pi, surv$time, surv$event, share_cutoff(pi, 0.25))
c(log_rank_p = signif(res$p, 3), auc = round(res$auc, 3))
```

```{r km}
fit <- survival::survfit(survival::Surv(surv$time, surv$event) ~ res$group)
plot(fit, col = c("#5fbf3f", "#3a54a5"), lwd = 2, mark.time = TRUE,
     xlab = "Time to relapse (years)", ylab = "Probability")
legend("bottomleft", c("Lower risk", "Higher risk"), col = c("#5fbf3f", "#3a54a5"), lwd = 2)
```

The clinical model of the paper on its training set:

```{r clinical_model}
x <- clinical_matrix(clin, c("er", "pgr", "p53", "grade", "node", "size_mm", "age"))
cm <- cox_lasso(x, clin$time, clin$event, runs = 20)
round(cm$coefficients, 3)
```

## Compare with the expected output

The paper's printed p-values for the training set, against ours:

```{r compare_paper}
paper <- read.csv(example_path("paper_values.csv"), colClasses = "character")
ours <- c(
  logrank_p(clin$time, clin$event, clin$node), logrank_p(clin$time, clin$event, clin$grade),
  logrank_p(clin$time, clin$event, clin$p53), logrank_p(clin$time, clin$event, clin$er),
  logrank_p(clin$time, clin$event, clin$pgr),
  univariate_cox(cbind(LN = clin$node, size = clin$size_mm, grade = clin$grade, p53 = clin$p53),
                 clin$time, clin$event)$p)
printed_digits <- function(s) {
  s <- tolower(s)
  if (grepl("e", s)) { p <- strsplit(s, "e")[[1]]; nchar(sub("^[^.]*\\.?", "", p[1])) - as.integer(p[2]) }
  else nchar(sub("^[^.]*\\.?", "", s))
}
paper$ours <- signif(ours, 4)
paper$match <- abs(ours - as.numeric(paper$value)) <= 0.5 * 10^(-sapply(paper$value, printed_digits)) + 1e-15
paper
cat(sum(paper$match), "of", nrow(paper), "p-values match the paper as printed\n")
stopifnot(all(paper$match))
```

For the synthetic data the expected output is the formula the data were drawn from: each score
should follow its set's activity, and the model should rank the sets as their true effects do.

```{r compare_truth}
truth <- read.csv(example_path("synthetic_truth.csv"))
effects <- read.csv(example_path("synthetic_effects.csv"))
r <- sapply(names(sets), function(k) cor(pds[k, ], truth[[k]]))
round(r, 3)
b <- model$coefficients[effects$set]; b[is.na(b)] <- 0
data.frame(set = effects$set, true_log_hr = effects$log_hazard_ratio, fitted = round(unname(b), 3))
cat(sum(r >= 0.9), "of 3 scores follow their activity; ranking matches:",
    identical(order(-b), order(-effects$log_hazard_ratio)), "\n")
stopifnot(all(r >= 0.9), identical(order(-b), order(-effects$log_hazard_ratio)))
```

## Your own data

- **Expression**: a genes by samples matrix of log2 values, gene symbols as row names (one row per
  gene; `probes_to_genes()` collapses Affymetrix probes with a GEO annotation file).
- **Gene sets**: a named list of symbol vectors (`read_gmt()` reads MSigDB files; the paper used the
  403 KEGG and BioCarta sets of MSigDB's C2 collection).
- **Survival**: time and event (1 = relapse) per sample, in the column order of the matrix.
- **Options that matter**: `pathway_scores(attempts =)` (pathifier's subsamplings; 100 by default),
  `cox_lasso(runs =, fold =)` (cross-validation runs and folds; the median of the runs' optimal
  penalties is used), and `share_cutoff(pi, share)` (the share of tumours called higher risk:
  0.25 in the paper, or a data set's relapse share).
- **Outputs**: `model$coefficients` are the selected features and their log hazard ratios;
  `evaluate_model()` returns the log-rank p-value, the AUC of the index against relapse, the risk
  groups and the ROC curve.

To score a new data set with a trained model, compute its scores with `pathway_scores()` and
apply `prognostic_index()` with the trained coefficients. Without normal samples, pathifier's
scores are computed within each data set, so a cutoff carried from one data set to another
assumes they are on the same scale.

The paper's four data sets, every table and figure and the comparison with the published values:
